html:
The war for control of Vietnam from 1955 to 1975, between communist North Vietnam and the South Vietnamese state backed by the United States. In Vietnam it is called the American War. It was the longest hot war of the Cold War.

After the French lost at Dien Bien Phu in 1954, a peace deal split Vietnam in two. The North was led by Ho Chi Minh. In the South, communist guerrillas, the Viet Cong, fought the government in Saigon, supplied by the North along the Ho Chi Minh Trail through Laos and Cambodia.

The United States sent advisers and then, from 1965, combat troops, over half a million at the peak. It bombed the North heavily. The Tet Offensive of 1968 failed on the battlefield but turned American opinion against the war. Protest spread, and the boxer Muhammad Ali refused the draft.

US forces left after the Paris Peace Accords of 1973. North Vietnamese tanks took Saigon on 30 April 1975 (fall of Saigon), and the country was united the next year. Estimates of Vietnamese dead run from about one to over three million; about 58,000 Americans died. The war spilled into Cambodia, where Pol Pot's Khmer Rouge took power in 1975, and its end set off the flight of the boat people.
